extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students of literature, and literary critics interested in biography, criticism, and creative-writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for assessing and composing literary biographies, travel sketches, lyric poetry, tragedy, and humor — using Heinrich Heine and German literature as exemplars. Emphasizes qualities of style, tone, appropriateness, and structural coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to gradations of perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Nicety of perception (fine gradations in time and feeling) is a national quality that affects appreciation and exhibition of humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay argues that lack of subtle perception (e.g., German 'insensibility to gradations in time') produces a different quality of humor: less delicate, more blunt. Use sensitivity to nuance as a criterion when judging humor's refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as 'flavor of mind' and pungent satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is the 'flavor of mind' pervading a writer's work and often concentrates itself into pungent satire (example: Lessing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether wit appears as an underlying intellectual tone across a writer's pieces and whether it crystallizes into effective satire. Example provided: Lessing's Hamburgische Dramaturgie showing concentrated pungent satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordplay and verbal quibble as one form of wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbal quibbles and wordplay (Wortspiel) are a recognizable form of wit, appreciable but not the only measure of literary brilliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize wordplay as a criterion of wit, but avoid taking it as the sole test of literary greatness; the essay cites Germans admiring Shakespeare chiefly for his Wortspiel as a partial and limited appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development from rough jests to refined epigram
rubrics_metrics.description: Pointless puns and stupid jocularity of youth may develop into epigrammatic brilliancy and polished playfulness in maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a writer's humor, consider developmental trajectory: juvenilia's faults can be seeds for mature wit. This is offered as a defense against dismissing early coarseness.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (European) standing as a measure of humor's quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A production's value in humor may be measured by whether it ranks as 'European' — i.e., contributes to the common stock of European wit and humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-cultural reach and influence (works being adopted or celebrated beyond their home nation) as a criterion for judging the quality or universality of comic writing; the essay notes Germany lacked such European comic contributions prior to the present century.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refined mental activity as source of high-quality humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Racy wit and chastened delicate humor are the inevitable results of invigorated and refined mental activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor works that show intellectual refinement and mental vigor when seeking delicate, high-order humor. Consider intellectual breadth and subtlety as prerequisites for certain kinds of humorous effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmuting folly into art (satirical alchemy)
rubrics_metrics.description: A great humorist or wit 'touches leaden folly with the magic wand of his fancy, and transmutes it into the fine gold of art.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge humorists by their ability to elevate base or foolish subjects into artful, illuminating comment — not merely to mock. Heine is praised for this transformative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of coarseness, scurrility, and personal license
rubrics_metrics.description: Coarseness, scurrility, and Mephistophelean contempt for reverent feelings detract from artistic value and can mingle with genius to weaken the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically weigh instances where powerful style expresses debased feeling; strong powers used for coarse personal attacks lower overall aesthetic worth. The essay recommends removing such elements for younger/immature readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-appropriateness and editorial censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Before placing works with coarse or scurrilous content within reach of immature minds, apply a strict friendly censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider age-appropriateness and the need to excise gratuitous coarseness before presenting certain works to broader or younger audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketch tone and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographies should avoid intrusive gossip and should derive coloring chiefly from autobiographical hints and the subject's own writings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing or evaluating a life-sketch, prioritize dignity and restraint: emphasize the subject's own materials and avoid gratuitous rumor. The essay explicitly states it will not hold the candle up to 'dusty, vermin-haunted corners.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyric poetry qualities: style, imagination, sensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Lyric excellence combines 'lightness and finish of style,' 'vivid and original imaginativeness,' and 'simple, pure sensibility' (example: Heine's Buch der Lieder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these three facets to evaluate lyrics: technical polish, imaginative originality, and sincere feeling. A deficiency in any may lessen the work's lyric appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel sketch composition: blending varied tones
rubrics_metrics.description: Good travel writing blends fun, imagination, reflection, and satire in an ever-varying shimmer (likened to the hues of the opal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess travel sketches for their ability to move fluidly among modes (humor, idyll, criticism, reverie) while keeping an integrated voice; balance of elements is a positive sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragedy/dramatic structure and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic works require characters who are more than shadowy vehicles for poetry and a structure marked by clearness and probability (critique of Heine's Almansor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating tragedies, look for believable motivations, defined characters, and a coherent plot structure; poetic passages do not compensate for lack of dramatic probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of anecdote as rhetorical device
rubrics_metrics.description: Anecdotes in sketches and memoirs are often devices of style used to convey satire or opinion rather than literal truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat anecdotal material critically: recognize when it may be stylized or invented for rhetorical effect, and evaluate its effectiveness in service of the writer's purpose rather than its factual accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical stance toward genius: emphasize the good over gratuitous denunciation
rubrics_metrics.description: When judging gifted figures, it is more edifying and cheering to appreciate their good rather than dwell lengthily on failings; critics often measure geniuses by arbitrary expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a charitable critical tone: resist 'overzealous' demands that geniuses perform beyond reasonable expectation; compare their actual output to ordinary standards rather than to speculative maxima.
